prompt: Marieke, the CFO, is preparing the board pack and asks which parent categories sold high-ticket order lines in 2025, and how much of their revenue came through the web. Use the sales table and the order lines with an order_date from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, both days included. Return four columns, in this order: parent_category; n_orders, the number of different orders (order_id) with at least one line in that parent category; revenue_eur, the sum of net_revenue_eur, not rounded; and web_revenue_pct, 100 times the net revenue of the lines with channel 'web' divided by revenue_eur, rounded to 1 decimal with ROUND(x, 1), so 15 percent is 15.0. A parent category with no web revenue has a web_revenue_pct of 0.0. A missing net_revenue_eur adds nothing to either total. Keep only the parent categories whose average net revenue per order line is above 150 euros; that average leaves out lines with a missing net_revenue_eur. Sort by revenue_eur from highest to lowest.
hints: Next, choose the table and the rows: the 2025 order lines in sales, then decide what one row stands for.
The web share needs a sum over the web lines only, with 0 for the other lines. The 150 euro test is on each group's average, so it comes after GROUP BY, not in WHERE.
why_this_works: HAVING tests each parent category's average line, and a conditional SUM with ELSE 0 gives the web revenue, 0 when there is none.
